doc.title: Hal Galper interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 27, 2022

title: Contributing tunes to Cannonball Adderley's band
summary: Galper spent two and a half years with Cannonball; he thinks his modern tunes were a mistake for what was basically a blues band.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: Your two years — it was just two years I guess.
Two and a half years it was.
Two and a half years — how did they — did they invite you to contribute to the band’s repertoire or did you lobby, like hey guys I have some tunes can we read them?
Yeah. They always needed tunes, they always needed music, but they always had piano players that wrote.

Yeah. Almost always. I don’t think Junior Mance wrote but I’m not sure about that. Bobby Timmons wrote for them, you know. But I think I made him — I’ve said this before — I think I made a mistake in judgment in the tunes that I gave the band because I was — this is really hard to explain but I’m a greedy son of a bitch. I just want to play as much as possible because I know that school you know. But I gave them — my tunes were too modern. I mean I’ve got — Cannonball could play anything and Nat could play anything but it was basically a blues band and I should have stuck both solo-wise and in the tunes I gave him I think I made a mistake. Now that I can look back at my career and I have all his recordings, I can make judgments about my judgments. You know? That was a mistake. I should have stayed more blues oriented.
